reason: The holdout is a genetic screen, so localisation is admissible as an input here; fitness inputs are excluded because the gra17 delta and phenotype columns are that same screen, and the BioID control is a third experiment.

question: Which proteins are tethered to membranes by palmitoylation rather than by a transmembrane segment?

question: Which proteins resist a single steady-state compartment because they are genuinely dual-localised or in transit, rather than merely scarce?
reason: Assignment confidence tracks how much protein there is, and protein abundance is an input, so the map may recover the label technically rather than biologically; I cannot judge the size of that confound from the two CSVs.

question: Can signal peptides, transmembrane segments and domain content place a protein in its compartment?
refusal: the validation holdout 'pvm_proximity_positive' is not independent of the primary 'compartment_best' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing

question: Which proteins carry a signal peptide?
refusal: the validation holdout 'is_tm' is not independent of the primary 'has_signal_peptide' -- shared experiment (plasmodb_pf3d7_attributes). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criterion 5: the label is already computable from sequence for all 8140 genes so nobody changes an experiment on the answer, and is_tm comes out of the same prediction pipeline, so it is not an independent control either.

question: Which effectors leave the parasite as soluble protein rather than packaged in vesicles?
reason: Only 165 genes carry the label; iedb_epitope_count at 221 was measured too sparse to put 15 labelled genes in any cluster, so this holdout cannot be evaluated at cluster level at all.

question: Which proteins are N-myristoylated and therefore anchored at the parasite periphery?
reason: 65 labelled genes with a minority class of 23 - an order of magnitude below what cluster-level evaluation needs, by the same sparsity limit measured on the epitope columns (criterion 2 in practice).

question: Which PVM proteins face the host cytosol rather than the vacuolar lumen?
refusal: the validation holdout 'compartment_best' is not independent of the primary 'pvm_proximity_positive' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Criterion 6: the only PVM column is a proximity yes/no and it carries no membrane-orientation information, so the question as asked has no label in the table - the recipe would silently answer a different question.

question: Which proteins were localised by hyperLOPIT directly rather than by orthoLOPIT transfer?
refusal: the validation holdout 'lopit_confident' is not independent of the primary 'compartment_source' -- shared experiment (lopit_tgon). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: This is provenance metadata - it records which pipeline made the call, so recovering it changes nobody's next experiment (criterion 5), and lopit_confident is the same experiment so the control is a copy too.

question: Which uncharacterised proteins are loaded into the oocyst, and are they the genes the sexual stages switch on?
reason: Protein-abundance inputs are excluded because the oocyst iTRAQ ratios live there; the control is a cat-gut RNA experiment, entirely independent of the oocyst proteome measurement, and both holdouts are dense (2068 and 4463 genes).

question: Which genes are needed to persist in the mouse brain at 14 days but are dispensable for growth in culture?
reason: Fitness inputs are excluded so neither screen leaks into the map; the IFN-gamma macrophage screen is a separate study from the in vivo brain screen, so it is a genuine second observation of chronic-stage pressure.

question: Which transcripts does the BFD2 switch hold, and are they the bradyzoite programme?
reason: RNA-abundance inputs are excluded so neither the RIP ratio nor the expression-derived stage call is fed in; stage_enriched_derived is exactly the trivially-recovering control the brief describes, used here as a control and not as a discovery.

question: Which mRNAs are held translationally silent as tachyzoites begin converting?
reason: The holdout is a single replicate whose RNA denominator sits in the excluded expression family, and I cannot tell from the CSVs whether translation-efficiency columns are addressed apart from RNA abundance; n_m6a_peaks at 837 genes and only 2 usable bins is borderline as a control.

question: Which genes are tachyzoite-, bradyzoite- or oocyst-enriched?
refusal: the validation holdout 'expr_cyst' is not independent of the primary 'stage_enriched_derived' -- declared family (Tg_transcription_bradyzoite_tissue_cyst). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: stage_enriched_derived is computed from the very expression columns being fed in, so it recovers trivially - it is a control, not a discovery (measured trap) - and expr_cyst is one of those input columns as well.

question: Can the single-cell expression programme assign each gene to a cell-cycle phase?
refusal: the validation holdout 'cellcycle_pseudotime' is not independent of the primary 'cellcycle_phase' -- declared family (Tg_cell_cycle_timing_label). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: cellcycle_phase is derived from single-parasite RNA-seq and lives under RNA abundance, so RNA inputs restate it (criterion 3); pseudotime is the same single-cell experiment, so the control is a copy as well (criterion 4).

question: Which genes are stage-restricted, checked against how sharply stage-restricted they are?
refusal: the validation holdout 'stage_margin_derived' is not independent of the primary 'stage_enriched_derived' -- declared family (Tg_life_cycle_stage_label_derived). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: stage_margin_derived is the margin behind the stage_enriched_derived call - the same computation twice on the same 1911 genes, so the control controls nothing (criterion 4).

question: Which genes respond to alkaline stress in the conversion reporter time course?
refusal: the validation holdout 'stress_6-16_stress_green_48' is not independent of the primary 'stress_5-24_stress_green_48' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: The holdout is one sample of the stress experiment whose sibling samples sit in the RNA inputs (restatement, criterion 3), and the control is another sample of that same experiment (criterion 4).

question: Which genes are required for an oocyst to sporulate?
reason: Criterion 6: every fitness screen in the table is tachyzoite or mouse, so there is no requirement label for sporulation - the only sporulation columns are abundance, and the recipe would quietly answer 'expressed in oocysts' instead.

question: Can measurements predict how many transcript models a gene has?
reason: Passes criteria 1-4 and fails 5: transcript-model count is an annotation artefact of how the gene was assembled, and no knockout, antibody or imaging decision turns on it.

question: What is the overall structure of stage conversion across the genome?
refusal: these inputs restate a holdout and were removed entirely rather than trimmed: biology: gene expression > RNA abundance
reason: Criterion 1: there is no wrong answer - any map produces 'structure', so nothing the recipe returns could contradict the question.

question: Which uncharacterised proteins sit inside clusters that are almost entirely one enzyme class, and therefore come with a pathway to test?
reason: Sequence and metabolic-pathway inputs are excluded because EC numbers are derived from them; hyperLOPIT is a separate experiment and pathway members should share a compartment, so the control is independent and dense (3855 genes).

question: Do the expanded Toxoplasma paralogue families actually behave as one unit, and which unassigned genes belong with them?
reason: Orthogroups are homology calls so every sequence input is barred; RNA is left out so the expression-derived stage control is not restated by the inputs, and family membership and stage restriction are independent facts about a gene.

question: Which Toxoplasma-specific genes behave like conserved core machinery, and are those the ones the parasite cannot lose?
reason: Sequence and orthology inputs are barred because the label is an orthology call; fitness is kept out so the CRISPR control stays independent of the map, and both holdouts cover the whole 8140-gene table.

question: Do the proteins whose phosphorylation goes up together form one signalling module - one that also shows up as calcium-responsive in thermal stability?
reason: PTM inputs are excluded because the phospho columns live there; CETSA calcium shift is a different experiment on a different readout, so a cluster agreeing on both is two observations, not one (1182 and 2348 genes labelled).

question: Which uncharacterised proteins co-melt with the subunits of known complexes?
reason: The control has only 494 labelled genes spread over four classes, close to the sparsity that was measured to break cluster evaluation at 221; and melting temperature may be a physical property more than a complex signal, which puts criterion 5 in doubt.

question: Which pairs of proteins physically bind each other?
reason: Criterion 6: a recipe assigns one label per gene and an edge between two genes is not a column; partner counts are the only per-gene stand-in and they answer 'how many partners', which is a different question.

question: Which genes are Toxoplasma-specific, checked against whether they have a Plasmodium ortholog?
refusal: the validation holdout 'has_pf_ortholog' is not independent of the primary 'lineage_specific' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: lineage_specific is defined by the same ortholog calls that produce has_pf_ortholog, so the control is a restatement of the primary (criterion 4) - the same failure mode as pairing two LOPIT views.

question: Can domain content place a gene in its orthogroup?
reason: Inputs and both holdouts come out of the same homology pipeline: the map restates the label (criterion 3) and pfam_id is a copy of the primary (criterion 4).

question: Which proteins have a reported interaction partner?
reason: Only 48 of 8140 genes are positive, so no cluster can hold the 15 labelled members an evaluation needs; and both columns record how often a gene was pulled into somebody's pulldown, not whether it has partners.

question: Which genes look like the ones that keep turning up in interaction studies?
reason: Both are study-participation counts - the attention_depth confound in another guise - so they measure what has been done to a gene rather than the gene (criterion 5), and they are not independent of each other (criterion 4).

question: Which understudied genes behave like the well-studied ones?
refusal: the validation holdout 'lit_tier' is not independent of the primary 'attention_depth' -- declared family (Tg_literature_attention). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: attention_depth is how much a gene has been written about and is a negative control only; recovering it reports publication bias rather than biology (criterion 5), and lit_tier comes from the same text mining (criterion 4).

question: Which uncharacterised genes sit inside the co-expressed, co-translated, co-complexed modules that the parasite cannot lose in culture?
reason: No fitness input, so the seven-screen trap is avoided; primary and control are separate experiments (HFF competitive screen vs an independent in vivo brain library) with 7325 and 7334 labelled genes.

question: Which genes are required for growth in interferon-gamma-activated macrophages but dispensable in resting ones?
refusal: the validation holdout 'fit_naive_bmdm' is not independent of the primary 'fit_ifng' -- shared experiment (crispr_macrophage). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criteria 3 and 4 together: the differential does not exist as a column, so asking it means feeding fit_naive_bmdm in as an input while holding out fit_ifng, and the two arms are one experiment measuring the same thing under two conditions.

question: Which genes are required for survival in the spleen specifically?
refusal: the validation holdout 'fit_invivo_liver' is not independent of the primary 'fit_invivo_spleen' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criterion 4: fit_invivo_spleen, liver, lung and PE are four organ readouts of one in vivo screen (all 7395 labelled), so a second organ is not a second observation.

question: Which genes become essential only when the PVM nutrient pore GRA17 is deleted - what backs up the parasite access to host nutrients?
reason: The delta column is already normalised against the parental screen so ordinary essentiality is not restated, no fitness category is fed in, and the control is a different screen entirely - crispr_gra17_candidate and crispr_gra17ko_phenotype are barred as controls because they are the same experiment.

question: Which genes are essential in a GRA17 knockout background?
reason: Fails criterion 5 and brushes criterion 3: the knockout-background fitness score is dominated by ordinary essentiality, so it re-derives fit_invitro_hff and changes nobody's next move; the informative column is the synthetic-lethal delta.

question: Which genes are required to persist in the brain during chronic infection but not during acute growth?
reason: No fitness input; the 14-day brain library and the acute in vivo organ screen are separate experiments with 7334 and 7395 labelled genes, and chronic-versus-acute is a real contrast between two independent screens rather than two arms of one.

question: Do host-interaction measurements alone predict which genes the parasite needs in a living animal?
reason: Fitness is kept out of the inputs, the map is built only from parasite-host relationship and expression data, and the control is a different in vivo screen from a different library, so agreement between them is a second observation rather than a copy.

question: Which uncharacterised genes cause a replication defect when knocked out?
reason: Criterion 2 is technically met but density is the doubt: only 318 genes carry the imaging-screen label, and the measured floor in this table is that a 221-gene column cannot fill a cluster with 15 labelled members - 318 is in the same band, and the sibling screens (actin, egress, apicoplast) cannot serve as the control because they are one experiment.

question: Can co-fitness and co-expression recover how many nonsynonymous SNPs a gene carries across strains?
refusal: the validation holdout 'snp_total_all_strains' is not independent of the primary 'snp_nonsynonymous' -- shared experiment (plasmodb_pf3d7_attributes). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criterion 5 exactly as the brief's own length example does, and fails criterion 4 as well: a SNP-count bin is not a list anyone picks a knockout or an antibody from, and total SNPs is the same count with the synonymous ones added back.

question: Are essential genes distinguishable by their codon adaptation and GC3 content?
refusal: the validation holdout 'codon_gc3' is not independent of the primary 'codon_cai_ribosomal' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criterion 5 and criterion 4: nobody acts on a CAI bin, and CAI, GC3 and ENC are three statistics computed from one sequence, so the control is a copy - this is the sequence-statistic trap for this axis.

question: Which of the genes hyperLOPIT could not assign are nonetheless required in vivo?
refusal: the validation holdout 'fit_hyperlopit_unassigned_invivo_lib2' is not independent of the primary 'fit_hyperlopit_unassigned_invivo_lib1' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criterion 4 and density at once: lib1 and lib2 are two libraries of one screen, and at 291 and 290 labelled genes neither can put 15 labelled members in a cluster.

question: Which essential genes are druggable - essential in vivo and absent from the human genome?
refusal: the holdout '' is not a column in this table
reason: Fails criterion 6: neither CSV has a human-orthology, druggability or compound-target column; has_pf_ortholog and has_cp_ortholog are apicomplexan orthology and answer a different question.

question: Which uncharacterised proteins behave like enzymes - as co-expressed, co-translated and fitness-coupled as the annotated enzyme set?
reason: Metabolism is excluded from the inputs because it contains the label, and so is sequence: EC numbers are assigned by homology, so pfam or interpro inputs would recover the label by predicting it, the same trap the brief names for localisation; the control is a single LOPIT view used alone, which the six-view refusal permits, and localisation is therefore kept out of the inputs.

question: Can expression and fitness data recover which enzyme class a protein belongs to?
reason: Only 11 EC classes reach 15 members and the top ones are kinases, phosphatases and acetyltransferases, so the label tests signalling annotation rather than pathway membership; those classes cover only a few hundred of the 1313 labelled genes and I cannot tell from the CSVs whether any cluster reaches 15 same-class members.

question: Which metabolic modules does the parasite need during infection of a living animal, and which uncharacterised genes cluster inside them?
reason: Metabolism is the input and fitness is the holdout, so the seven-screen trap does not apply; primary and control are separate screens (in vivo organ library vs the HFF competitive screen) and both are densely labelled.

question: Which genes buffer oxidative stress - what does the parasite need when its redox metabolism is challenged?
reason: Neither fitness nor chemical response is admitted as an input, so the score cannot be recovered from general essentiality; the macrophage screen is an independent experiment in which the same redox genes should matter. Residual risk: if the score is a raw dropout rather than a stress-normalised one, general essentiality leaks into the label itself.

question: Which genes act in the apicoplast type II fatty acid synthesis pathway?
reason: Fails criterion 6 as asked: neither CSV carries a pathway-membership column, and the only proxy - the compartment label - is the LOPIT localisation experiment, which turns a metabolism question into a localisation recipe answering something else.

question: Do metabolite levels track the expression of the enzymes that produce them?
refusal: the holdout '' is not a column in this table
reason: Fails criterion 6: there are no metabolomics columns in either CSV, so there is nothing to hold out - the table measures genes, not metabolites.

question: Which transporters import which host-derived nutrients?
reason: Fails criteria 3 and 6: transporter identity exists in this table only inside interpro and pfam annotation, which is sequence-derived, so any map admitting sequence recovers the class by predicting it, and no substrate or transport-assay column exists at all.

question: Which metabolic enzymes are lysine-acetylated, linking them to acetyl-CoA availability?
reason: Fails criterion 5 because absence is not a class: only proteins that have sites are labelled, so the holdout separates site-count strata among already-acetylated proteins rather than acetylated from unacetylated. The same defect sinks n_nitrosylation_sites, n_lactylation_sites, n_ubiquitination_sites and n_o_fucosyl_peptides.

question: Which proteins are intrinsically thermostable in the parasite proteome?
reason: Fails criterion 4 and criterion 5: the melting temperature and the calcium shift score are two readouts of one thermal-proteome experiment, and a Tm bin on its own changes nobody's next experiment.

question: Which proteins change thermal stability in the presence of calcium - which are the candidate calcium-regulated enzymes?
reason: The question itself is actionable (a pulldown list of candidate Ca2+-binding proteins) but the only independent control I can find is the phosphoproteome at 1175 labelled genes, and I cannot tell whether that puts 15 labelled members in any cluster; the melting temperature column is barred as a control because it is the same experiment.

question: Which metabolic enzymes switch on in sporulated oocysts?
reason: Fails criterion 3 twice over: the oocyst iTRAQ columns measure the same stage on the other molecule, so the control restates the primary, and expr_sporulated itself sits inside gene expression > RNA abundance, which the map would have to admit as an input to work at all.

question: Can the map recover how many synonymous SNPs or how long an enzyme is?
refusal: the validation holdout 'length' is not independent of the primary 'snp_synonymous' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criterion 5, stated explicitly because it is the standing trap for this axis: snp_synonymous, snp_total_all_strains, codon_enc, codon_gc3, length and mean_plddt all pass criteria 1 to 4 and change nothing about what anyone does next.

question: Which transcripts does the bradyzoite RNA-binding regulator BFD2 hold - which mRNAs are its targets beyond the known ones?
reason: The RIP value is IP-over-input, so transcript abundance is normalised out and the RNA inputs do not restate it; the HDAC3 CUT&Tag control is a different molecule, assay and laboratory, and both are densely labelled (7463 and 8140).

question: Which genes are held silent in tachyzoites by chromatin and released in the cat-gut enteroepithelial stages?
reason: No expression input, so the holdout differential is not fed back in; primary and control are two independent sexual-stage datasets (7739 vs 4463 labelled, so different studies) that should agree if the tachyzoite repression model is right, and fitness is a legal input because the holdout is not a fitness screen.

question: Do fitness, localisation and interaction data alone tell you which promoters the HDAC3 repressor occupies?
reason: Expression is deliberately excluded because accessibility and occupancy track transcript level directly, which is the same predicts-the-label trap the brief names for sequence and localisation; what remains - dispensability plus secretory localisation - is real biology, and the control is an independent in vivo expression measurement that is not an input.

question: Which promoters are open, and can expression data tell you?
reason: Fails criterion 3: promoter accessibility tracks transcript abundance, so an RNA-fed map recovers the ATAC label by predicting it rather than by finding biology - the same trap the brief names for sequence features and localisation. The H4ac control has the same defect.

question: Which genes carry active-chromatin histone marks?
reason: Fails criterion 4: HDAC3 is the enzyme that removes histone acetylation, so the control is the mechanistic inverse of the primary and not an independent observation; the RNA input also makes it the accessibility-tracks-expression trap again.

question: Which genes are derepressed when the MORC repressor is degraded?
refusal: the validation holdout 'morc_MORC_UT1' is not independent of the primary 'morc_MORC_IAA1' -- shared experiment (morc_depletion). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criteria 4 and 6 as posed: the morc_* columns are per-sample RNA abundances for each genotype, not a depletion contrast, so a single sample binned in three encodes expression level and any two of them are one experiment - the derepression log-fold-change the question needs is not a column.

question: Which transcripts depend on CPSF4 for correct polyadenylation?
refusal: the validation holdout 'cpsf4rna168155_ut_1' is not independent of the primary 'cpsf4rna168155_iaa_24h_1' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Same defect as the MORC recipe: cpsf4rna168155_* are per-sample abundances at 7, 24 and 48 hours of auxin plus untreated, the IAA-versus-UT contrast is not a column, and pairing two samples as primary and control is one experiment (criterion 4).

question: Which uncharacterised proteins are transcription factors of the AP2 family?
refusal: the validation holdout 'interpro_id' is not independent of the primary 'pfam_id' -- shared experiment (interpro). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criteria 3 and 4: the only transcription-factor label in this table is the AP2 domain inside pfam_id and interpro_id, which is sequence-derived, so the class is recovered by prediction, and the two annotation columns are the same assignment under two databases.

question: Which genes are cell-cycle regulated, built from protein and chromatin data rather than RNA?
refusal: the validation holdout 'cellcycle_pseudotime' is not independent of the primary 'cellcycle_phase' -- declared family (Tg_cell_cycle_timing_label). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: Fails criterion 4: phase and pseudotime are two readouts of one single-parasite RNA-seq experiment. The only independent cell-cycle columns, the cellcycle19092 bulk time course, are per-timepoint abundances whose three-bin split encodes expression level rather than phase, so no legal control exists.

question: Which uncharacterised genes belong to the BFD1 and MORC controlled bradyzoite regulon?
reason: I cannot tell from the CSVs how much of the gene regulation category is accessibility and acetylation data that tracks transcript level directly; if it dominates, the chromatin inputs recover the expression holdout by prediction rather than by biology, which is the same objection that sinks the ATAC recipe run in the other direction.

question: Which transcripts are destabilised by m6A methylation?
reason: Fails on density and criterion 4: at 412 labelled genes the primary sits in the band where the measured 221-gene floor bites, and m6A peak count is the mechanistic cause of the decay the primary measures, so the control is close to a copy rather than an independent observation.

question: Which uncharacterised proteins behave like PVM-resident effectors - which unlabelled genes fall in map clusters dominated by proteins detected at the parasitophorous vacuole membrane?
reason: keep - pvm_proximity_positive has 1274 labelled genes in 2 classes of >=15 and leaves 6866 unlabelled to nominate; the control is a CRISPR synthetic-lethal screen (7553 labelled), a different experiment from the proximity labelling, and no input carries interaction, proximity or provenance data. Two caveats stated up front: at 15.7% labelled only clusters of roughly 100+ genes will carry the >=15 labelled genes needed to score, and the control's positive class is only 118 genes so it can confirm but rarely contradict.

question: Which unlabelled genes belong to the parasitophorous-vacuole nutrient-pore network - which genes sit in clusters enriched for a large fitness delta in a GRA17 knockout background?
reason: keep - 7553 labelled at 3 bins, 587 unlabelled to nominate; the control is proximity labelling at the PVM (1274 labelled), a physically different assay from a pooled CRISPR screen; all genetic-screen and fitness input categories are excluded so nothing restates the delta. It is deliberately the reciprocal of the PVM recipe: the two use the same pair of columns in opposite roles and should agree, which is a coherence check, not a duplicate claim.

question: Which genes does the parasite need to survive inside a macrophage - which unlabelled genes cluster with the set whose loss costs fitness in naive bone-marrow-derived macrophages?
reason: keep - fit_naive_bmdm has 7402 labelled at 3 bins with 738 unlabelled to nominate, and the control is a transcript-level measurement labelled for all 8140 genes, so it can be scored on every cluster. The control is a different measurement type from the primary, which is the strongest form of independence available on this axis. RNA inputs are excluded because they would restate the expression control, and all genetic-screen and fitness inputs are excluded because they would restate the primary.

question: Which proteins face the host cell, built from the parasite-host interactome together with proximity data?
reason: drop - criterion 3: pvm_proximity_positive IS a parasite-host proximity measurement, so parasite-host relational inputs contain the holdout; the map would recover the label by carrying it rather than by finding biology. The same recipe with those two input categories removed is the keep above.

question: Can the map recover which genes are GRA17 synthetic-lethal candidates, validated against the size of the GRA17 fitness delta?
refusal: the validation holdout 'crispr_gra17_synthlethal_delta' is not independent of the primary 'crispr_gra17_candidate' -- shared experiment (gra17_synthlethal). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: drop - criterion 4: crispr_gra17_candidate and crispr_gra17_synthlethal_delta both carry 7553 labelled genes because they are the call and the effect size from one GRA17 synthetic-lethal screen. A control that is a thresholded copy of the primary controls nothing - the same failure mode as the six LOPIT views.

question: Which genes become essential when the PV pore is lost - which unlabelled genes cluster with the GRA17-knockout fitness phenotype, checked against baseline fitness in fibroblasts?
reason: uncertain - the existence of crispr_gra17_synthlethal_delta implies crispr_gra17ko_phenotype (7553 labelled) is differenced against a wild-type fitness arm, and fit_invitro_hff (7325 labelled) is the obvious candidate for that arm; if it is, this pairs a screen with its own baseline and fails criterion 4, the stage_enriched_derived trap in another guise. The labelled counts differ (7553 vs 7325) so I cannot show from the CSVs that they are or are not one experiment. Resolve by checking whether the delta column equals gra17ko_phenotype minus fit_invitro_hff.

question: Which parasite genes drive the host cell's transcriptional response to infection?
refusal: the validation holdout 'hosttx_padj' is not independent of the primary 'hosttx_T2' -- shared experiment (hosttx_effectors). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: drop - twice blocked. hosttx_T2 and hosttx_padj each have 252 labelled genes (3.1% of 8140), so a cluster needs about 480 genes before it carries the 15 labelled genes required to score, and they are the statistic and the p-value of one host-transcriptome experiment, so as a pair they fail criterion 4. Acquisition target: extend host-response profiling from 252 parasite genes to a genome-scale perturbation-by-host-transcriptome matrix, and add a second, independent host-response readout (e.g. host proteomics) to serve as control.

question: Which effectors are exported as soluble cargo rather than in vesicles - which unlabelled genes cluster with the soluble half of the secretome?
reason: drop - secretome_soluble_over_vesicle_log2 has 165 labelled genes (2.0%); no cluster short of about 740 genes carries the 15 labelled genes needed to score it, and the table holds no second secretion-route label to control with, so the recipe has no validation half at all. Acquisition target: genome-scale secretome/vesicle fractionation, plus any independent export-route assay (e.g. selective permeabilisation or a reporter export screen) as control.

question: Which unlabelled genes are needed for egress from the host cell - which genes cluster with the egress-defective hits from the imaging screen?
refusal: the validation holdout 'screen_replication_phenotype' is not independent of the primary 'screen_egress_phenotype' -- shared experiment (splitcas9_imaging_screen). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: drop - criterion 4 plus sparsity. All five screen_* columns carry exactly 318 labelled genes because they are five phenotypes scored in ONE 318-gene imaging screen, so primary and control are one experiment; and 318 labelled (3.9%) means clusters below about 385 genes abstain on both halves. Acquisition target: a genome-scale egress screen, and an independent egress readout from a different platform for the control.

question: Which genes act with GRA12 to keep the vacuole intact in vivo - which unlabelled genes cluster with the GRA12 screen hits?
refusal: the validation holdout 'crispr_gra12s2_l2fc_invivo' is not independent of the primary 'crispr_gra12s1_l2fc_invivo' -- shared experiment (gra12). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: drop - 236 and 232 labelled genes (about 2.9%) put both halves far below the 15-labelled-genes-per-cluster floor, and s1/s2 are two sublibraries of one GRA12 screen, so they are one experiment (criterion 4). This is the same shape of failure as the epitope columns: a real, interesting label that only covers a targeted gene set. Acquisition target: run the GRA12-background screen at genome scale.

question: Which genes are transcriptionally tuned to the macrophage niche - can the map recover macrophage expression rank?
reason: drop - criteria 1 and 5: macrophage_expression_percentile is labelled for all 8140 genes, so there are no unlabelled genes for the map to nominate and the recipe can only re-describe a measurement that already exists for every gene. It cannot come back with a gene list anyone would act on. A fully labelled column like this is fine as a CONTROL (it scores on every cluster) and useless as a primary.

question: Which proteins are host-interaction hubs, using the number of BioID studies that recovered a protein as the label?
reason: drop - n_bioid_studies counts how often a protein has been pulled into someone's proximity experiment; it is the attention_depth trap wearing a host-interaction label, and a hit here means the protein was studied, not that it is a hub. It is also labelled for all 8140 genes, so nothing can be nominated, and it shares its underlying assay with the pvm_proximity_positive control, so the pair is not independent either.

question: Are the lineage-specific genes the effectors - can functional measurements predict which genes lack apicomplexan orthologs?
reason: drop - three ways. lineage_specific is labelled for all 8140 genes so there is nothing to nominate; it is computed from has_pf_ortholog/has_cp_ortholog so the control is its own input (criterion 4); and the sequence-structure-and-evolution input category holds the orthology columns themselves, restating the holdout (criterion 3).

question: Which proteins respond to the calcium signal that triggers egress - which unlabelled genes cluster with the calcium-shifted thermal-stability set?
reason: drop - the primary half is fine (cetsa_calcium_ed_score has 2348 labelled at 3 bins with 5792 genes left to nominate) but the ONLY independent egress label in the table, screen_egress_phenotype, has 318 labelled genes (3.9%) and will abstain on essentially every cluster, so the recipe has no validation. This one is a single acquisition away from being a keep: a genome-scale egress or motility screen would turn it into a strong question.

question: Which parasite proteins change abundance across the first 48 hours of infection - which unlabelled genes cluster with the strongly regulated set?
refusal: the validation holdout 'proteome_log2_normalized_and_imputated_abundances_T_48h_R1' is not independent of the primary 'proteome_lfc_UT_Vs_T_24h_log2_fold_change' -- shared experiment (proteome_total). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: uncertain - I cannot tell from the CSVs what UT vs T is: untreated vs infected HOST cells, or an untreated vs treated parasite culture. If the rows are host genes the question is not answerable on this table at all (criterion 6); if they are parasite proteins the primary is viable at 3005 labelled with 5135 to nominate. Separately, the control I named is certainly wrong - the abundance and log-fold-change columns share the 3005-gene footprint of one proteomics run (criterion 4), so a kept version would need a control from a different experiment entirely.

question: Which uncharacterised genes are required to survive inside IFN-gamma-activated macrophages - which unlabelled genes cluster with the immune-evasion arsenal?
reason: keep - fit_ifng has 7402 labelled at 3 bins and leaves 738 unlabelled to nominate, so it scores on any cluster of about 20 genes; the control is a separate in-vivo tissue selection (7395 labelled) rather than the paired naive-macrophage arm of the same screen, and every fitness and genetic-screen input category is excluded so nothing restates the label. This is the densest genuinely immunological label in the table and is the main reason this axis is not entirely blocked. Residual risk to state: both halves are pooled CRISPR screens, so the independence is of experiment, not of method. [re-axed: its holdout is a fitness screen, not an immunity measurement]

question: Which genes are needed specifically when macrophages are activated - can the map separate the IFN-gamma requirement from the baseline macrophage requirement?
refusal: the validation holdout 'fit_naive_bmdm' is not independent of the primary 'fit_ifng' -- shared experiment (crispr_macrophage). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: drop - criterion 4: fit_ifng and fit_naive_bmdm both carry 7402 labelled genes because they are the treated and untreated arms of one macrophage screen. Two arms of one experiment are not two observations, and here they are worse than a copy - the biology of interest is the difference between them, so a cluster that recovers one recovers the other by construction.

question: Which genes are selected against during chronic infection of the brain - which unlabelled genes cluster with the genes the parasite needs to persist under immune control?
reason: keep - brain168465_14d_lfc has 7334 labelled at 3 bins with 806 unlabelled to nominate; the control is a different in-vivo screen (peritoneal exudate, 7395 labelled) from a different accession, and the primary's own 1d/2d/4d/7d timepoints are deliberately NOT used as control because they are the same screen. Inputs carry no fitness or screen data. The two niches differ enough (chronic CNS vs acute peritoneum) that the control can genuinely fail. [re-axed: its holdout is a fitness screen, not an immunity measurement]

question: Which unlabelled genes defend the parasite against oxidative attack - which genes cluster with the hits from the oxidative-stress screen?
reason: keep - oxidative_stress_screen_score has 7384 labelled at 3 bins with 756 unlabelled to nominate; the control is a different challenge in a different system (cytokine-activated macrophages vs a chemical oxidative challenge) and the expectation that ROS-defence genes also matter in activated macrophages is a real prediction that can come back false. Genetic-screen, fitness and chemical-response input categories are all excluded so neither half is restated. [re-axed: its holdout is a fitness screen, not an immunity measurement]

question: Which genes are under selection in host tissue but not in culture, and are they the genes the parasite also up-regulates in the macrophage niche?
reason: keep - and it is the best-controlled question on this axis because primary and control are different measurement types: fit_invivo_liver is a CRISPR fitness screen (7395 labelled, 745 unlabelled to nominate) and macrophage_expression_percentile is a transcript rank labelled for all 8140 genes, so the control scores on every cluster and cannot be a restatement of the primary. RNA inputs are excluded because they would restate the control; screen and fitness inputs are excluded because they would restate the primary. [re-axed: its holdout is a fitness screen, not an immunity measurement]

question: Which uncharacterised proteins are antigenic - which unlabelled genes fall in clusters dominated by proteins with catalogued T-cell epitopes?
reason: drop - the label exists but is too sparse to score. iedb_epitope_count is labelled for 221 of 8140 genes (2.7%) and collapses to only 2 classes when binned into 3; a cluster needs >=15 labelled genes to be evaluated at all, which at that density means a cluster of about 550 genes, and in a measured run on this table no cluster reached it - the epitope column abstained on every cluster. This is the single most damaging gap on this axis: the biologically obvious question is unanswerable for want of coverage, not for want of a method. Acquisition target: genome-scale epitope mapping - MHC immunopeptidomics of infected cells, or proteome-wide peptide arrays - to lift labelled genes from 221 to at least a couple of thousand, which is where cluster scoring starts to work.

question: Which proteins carry B-cell epitopes - which unlabelled genes cluster with the antibody-recognised set?
reason: drop - criterion 2, outright. n_bcell_epitopes has 34 labelled genes and appears in NEITHER inventory CSV, meaning it does not even form two classes of >=15 members, so it is not a legal holdout and is not answerable from this table (criterion 6). Acquisition target: a proteome-wide B-cell epitope or seroreactivity dataset; nothing short of that makes this column usable in any role, primary or control.

question: Which proteins carry both T-cell and B-cell epitopes - the shortlist a vaccine programme would start from?
refusal: the validation holdout 'n_bcell_epitopes' is not independent of the primary 'iedb_epitope_count' -- measured association. A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: drop - doubly blocked, and worth recording as the worst case on this axis. The primary has 221 labelled genes (2.7%) and abstains on almost every cluster; the control has 34 labelled genes, fails the >=2 classes of >=15 test entirely, and is explicitly refused as a validation holdout in the brief. Both halves need new data before the question exists, so it cannot be rescued by swapping inputs or bins.

question: Which unannotated genes behave like SRS surface antigens - which domainless genes cluster with the SRS/SAG family by expression and behaviour rather than by sequence?
reason: drop - the control kills it, not the primary. iedb_epitope_count (221 labelled) is explicitly refused as a validation holdout because no cluster reaches the 15 control-labelled genes needed to evaluate. The primary half is genuinely viable: interpro_desc has 4957 labelled with SRS-domain classes among its largest, leaves 3183 domainless genes to nominate, and with only expression and regulation inputs nothing sequence-derived restates it. Record it as one dense antigenicity label away from being a keep - the same acquisition that unblocks the epitope questions unblocks this one.

question: Which domainless genes are surface antigens - validated against where the LOPIT map puts them?
reason: drop - criterion 4: an SRS/SAG domain call all but determines a plasma-membrane or secretory LOPIT assignment, so compartment_best is a downstream consequence of the primary rather than an independent observation of the same biology - confirming it would confirm nothing. The brief's own trap note makes the direction explicit: sequence-derived labels predict localisation. Any sequence-derived input would additionally restate interpro_desc (criterion 3).

question: Which genes are immune-recognised, built from the host-immunity relational measurements?
refusal: these inputs restate a holdout and were removed entirely rather than trimmed: evidence: relational measurements > host immunity; biology: host recognition > stage-unspecified
reason: drop - criterion 3 on top of the sparsity. The epitope counts are what the host-immunity relational category contains, so those inputs restate the holdout and the map would recover the label by carrying it; and with 221 labelled genes (2.7%) it could not be scored even if the inputs were clean. This also records a structural fact about the axis: the only host-immunity input block in the table is the same 221-gene block that would have to be the holdout, so inputs and label cannot be separated here.

question: Which genes are antigenic, predicted from how heavily they have been studied?
refusal: these inputs have no columns in this build: biology: provenance and analysis metadata > stage-unspecified
reason: drop - the attention trap, twice. attention_depth and lit_tier measure how much a gene has been written about and are never inputs; worse, epitope curation is itself a function of study depth, so any apparent success is a publication artefact rather than immunology. lit_tier is also not independent of the primary for exactly that reason (criterion 4), and the 221-gene primary is unscoreable regardless.

question: Which genes are needed late rather than early during brain infection - which unlabelled genes cluster with the 14-day dropouts, checked against day 1?
refusal: the validation holdout 'brain168465_1d_lfc' is not independent of the primary 'brain168465_14d_lfc' -- shared experiment (gse168465). A control that is a copy controls nothing
reason: drop - criterion 4: brain168465 1d/2d/4d/7d/14d are timepoints of ONE in-vivo brain screen (labelled counts step down 6908/7055/7369/7393/7334 as coverage drops with time, not because they are different studies). Two readouts of one experiment are not two observations. The keep-shaped version of this question uses fit_invivo_PE, a different screen, as the control.

question: Which proteins are recognised by antibodies from chronically infected people - the seroreactive proteome?
refusal: the holdout '' is not a column in this table
reason: drop - criterion 6: there is no seroreactivity or serology column anywhere in either inventory. The nearest thing, iedb_epitope_count (221 genes), is a curation of previously published epitopes rather than a genome-wide measurement, and n_bcell_epitopes (34 genes) is smaller still. Acquisition target, and the highest-value one for this axis: a proteome-wide serological array run against human chronic-infection sera - it would supply both a dense primary and, alongside T-cell epitope mapping, the independent control that every other antigenicity question here is missing.

question: Which genes are immune-visible in vivo - do host-recognition annotations plus protein abundance predict which genes are selected against in the spleen?
reason: uncertain - the holdout and control are both fine (7395 and 8140 labelled, different measurement types), but I cannot tell from the CSVs which columns sit under 'host recognition > stage-unspecified'. If that address holds the 221-gene IEDB block it contributes almost nothing at 2.7% coverage and the recipe collapses into a protein-abundance recipe wearing an immunology label; if it holds a dense host-recognition annotation it is a keep as written. Resolve by listing the columns mapped to that address before running it - a guess either way costs more than the abstention.
